newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe company plans cellular payphones.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe company plans cellular payphones.

text.p: Cosmos Cellular (Pvt) Ltd has signed an agreement in principle with South Africa's Maxtel Ltd to set up a joint venture to provide a cellular payphone network in Zimbabwe.

Cosmos managing director Chemist Siziba told Reuters on Tuesday, "It is an innovation within the cellular industry. Through this we can reach out to the people who can't actually afford their own cellular phone.

"A cell phone is a cell phone and you can use it anywhere. In a call box, in a taxi. We will be using ordinary coin boxes to provide the service to the public using the cell phone advantage we have," he added.
Cosmos and Maxtel would each have a 50 percent stake in the venture which, in addition to the payphone network, planned to install cellular phones in taxis.

Siziba said the payphone network was viable because all it entailed was taking an ordinary cell phone line and repackaging it for use in a coin box, sidestepping the long delays associated with installing land lines.

Cosmos's cellular service network, currently confined to Harare, was likely to have expanded to the second largest city of Bulawayo by March -- connecting all towns along the main highway -- and to the rest of the country by June, Siziba said.
In addition to Cosmos there are two other cellular service providers, also operating on behalf of the state's Post and Telecommunications.
